<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard binary package for `kopuz-bin`, sourcing a prebuilt tarball from the project's official GitHub releases. The `source` array uses a direct HTTPS URL to download a versioned release archive, which is a normal and expected practice for binary packages. The checksum is explicitly provided and not set to 'SKIP', indicating intent to verify the downloaded file.

No `pkgver()` function is present, so no dynamic version resolution occurs during sourcing. The top-level scope contains only static declarations (variables, arrays, comments) with no command substitutions, external executions, or network operations. There are no `eval`, `curl`, `wget`, or similar calls in the global scope or anywhere else that could execute during `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`.

The package fetches from a trusted upstream (GitHub.com/Kopuz-org/kopuz) over HTTPS, and no code is executed during the source download phase. All operations in `package()` are deferred until later stages, which are not executed under the current command flags.

Thus, running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` is safe: it will only download and extract the specified tarball after verifying its checksum, and source the PKGBUILD without executing any potentially harmful commands.
</details>

<summary>
No dangerous code executes during source fetch</summary>
</security_assessment>
